title: 7.19.2 Sub-build: A list of kinds becomes a list of objects
description: KINDS is a list of plain { name, hp } objects; map turns it into a list of Monsters, and N moves which one you are looking at, stopping at the last.

steps.title: Run it
steps.instructions: The top says `Monster 1 of 1: Bat (6 hp)`. There are three kinds in `KINDS`, but `setup()` makes only one monster, by hand. N does nothing yet.

steps.title: One monster per kind
steps.instructions: In `setup()`, replace the line `monsters = [new Monster('Bat', 6)];` with `monsters = KINDS.map((k) => new Monster(k.name, k.hp));`. Run: `Monster 1 of 3`.
hints: `map` calls the function once for each kind, `k`, and collects each new Monster into a new list (3.7.2).
A loop that pushes a `new Monster(...)` for every kind does the same job.

steps.title: Next
steps.instructions: In `draw()`, below `background(...)`: `if (kb.presses('n') && which < monsters.length - 1) which += 1;`. Run and press N: the Wolf, then the Troll, and then it stays on the Troll. Add a fourth kind to `KINDS`, such as `{ name: 'Dragon', hp: 60 },`, and Run: `of 4`, with no other change.
hints: The last monster is `monsters.length - 1`: a list of 3 is numbered 0, 1 and 2.

requirements.title: A list of kinds becomes a list of objects
requirements.description: Every kind in KINDS becomes a new Monster, with map or a loop. Help: 7.19.1 (Reading: Kinds as data, map, and levelling up)

requirements.title: N moves to the next one
requirements.description: N adds 1 to which, and stops at the last monster in the list. Help: 7.19.1 (Reading: Kinds as data, map, and levelling up)
